[Who we are]{.ctric-section-tag}

## A national hub for tick science

[CTRIC is a dedicated research and commercial laboratory housed within Acadia University's Huestis Innovation Pavilion. We bring together leading researchers, government partners, and industry to tackle one of Canada's fastest-growing public health challenges. Ticks and Lyme disease now affect thousands of Canadians each year, with case counts nearly doubling between 2022 and 2024. Climate change is accelerating tick range expansion — and Canada needs a domestic centre of excellence to respond.]{.ctric-section-sub}

::: {.ctric-card-grid}

::: {.ctric-card}
**🔬 Built on proven expertise**

Our team has secured millions in external research funding and actively contributes to national surveillance networks including TickNet and e-Tick, in collaboration with the Public Health Agency of Canada and CanLyme.
:::

::: {.ctric-card}
**🏘️ Rooted in Atlantic Canada**

Located in Wolfville, NS, CTRIC creates skilled employment in rural Atlantic Canada while delivering national and international impact through research, innovation, and strategic partnerships.
:::

::: {.ctric-card}
**🛡️ Biosafety first**

CTRIC is built to Containment Level 2 (CL2) standards and registered with the Public Health Agency of Canada, ensuring the highest level of safety for staff, partners, and the environment.
:::

::: {.ctric-card}
**🔄 Reducing foreign dependency**

Canada currently relies on the Oklahoma State University facility for tick supply. CTRIC provides a Canadian-reared, locally relevant alternative — keeping research dollars at home and ensuring genetic relevance.
:::

:::

:::
:::

## Three core service streams

[CTRIC will offers specialized, fee-for-service capabilities to universities, government agencies, and industry partners across Canada and internationally.]{.ctric-section-sub}

:::: {.ctric-pillar}
<i class="bi bi-check-circle-fill"></i>

::: {.ctric-pillar-body}
**Tick rearing & supply**

Large-scale rearing of *Ixodes scapularis* (blacklegged tick) and *Dermacentor variabilis* (American dog tick) using artificial feeding systems — no live animals required. Canadian-reared ticks for academic, government, and commercial clients, with distribution beginning soon.
:::
::::

:::: {.ctric-pillar}
<i class="bi bi-check-circle-fill"></i>

::: {.ctric-pillar-body}
**Pathogen testing & diagnostics**

PCR-based molecular testing for Lyme disease (*Borrelia* spp.), *Anaplasma*, *Babesia*, *Rickettsia*, and other emerging tick-borne pathogens. Fee-for-service testing for researchers, health agencies, and commercial partners.
:::
::::

:::: {.ctric-pillar}
<i class="bi bi-check-circle-fill"></i>

::: {.ctric-pillar-body}
**Repellency & acaricidal testing**

Controlled laboratory evaluation of acaricides and repellents under standardized conditions. Supports Health Canada PMRA product registration and new product development for industry partners, including start-ups and established repellent and veterinary health companies.
:::
::::

:::::
::::::

## CTRIC and its amenities

[Our Containment Level 2 facility within Acadia's Huestis Innovation Pavilion is purpose-built for tick research — from colony maintenance and live tick supply to pathogen diagnostics and product testing.]{.ctric-section-sub}

::: {.ctric-amenity-grid .three-col}

::: {.ctric-amenity-card}
[🪲 Tick rearing]{.ctric-amenity-header}

We maintain year-round colonies of *Ixodes scapularis* and *Dermacentor variabilis* under controlled conditions, producing healthy, pathogen-screened ticks at every life stage. Our facility can supply ticks on a regular basis to research institutions, government agencies, and commercial partners, with the scale and consistency needed to support long-term programs.
:::

::: {.ctric-amenity-card}
[🧬 Tick pathogen testing]{.ctric-amenity-header}

We offer fast, reliable detection of tick-borne pathogens — including *Borrelia* spp., *Anaplasma*, *Babesia*, and *Rickettsia* — in ticks submitted by researchers, public health agencies, and surveillance programs. Results support disease monitoring, risk mapping, and research across Canada.
:::

::: {.ctric-amenity-card}
[🧴 Repellency testing]{.ctric-amenity-header}

We test repellents, treated fabrics, and acaricidal formulations against live ticks under standardized laboratory conditions. Our testing generates the efficacy data needed for Health Canada PMRA registration and supports the development of new products from early-stage research through to regulatory submission.
:::

:::

:::
:::
